summary: THE CLIENT HAS CHURNED. On 2026-09-21 at 12:55 Kirsten wrote: 'Hey guys, I’ve decided to go another way with my account. Thank you for everything you guys have been great, I just got an opportunity I can’t pass up! Please send me the final invoice I’ll get that paid straight away ❤️'. That is the last message in the file. Nobody from ALTR has replied to it. As of the window close on 2026-09-25 09:08 the termination notice has sat unanswered for 3 days and 20 hours, no final invoice has been sent, no save attempt has been made, and Derrek has not posted in this chat since 2026-09-13. Twelve messages this window, nine of them hers, three of them ours, and the whole account ended inside a ninety-minute span on a Monday morning. The sequence is worth reading exactly as it happened, because it is a textbook exit. At 11:24 she finally answered Ollie's Sept 18 wall-photo request — the fourth such request since July — with the same pushback she gave him in July: 'You should have loads still on the folders I sent you? Has that been all used up?'. Ollie replied 'Yes a lot of it has been used up'. She was accommodating anyway: 'I see well I am away atm I’ll try get some done when I am back next week is that okay?', then checked the brief herself — 'I can’t do do revealing because OFTV get annoyed right', 'So just normal clothes just fit ?' — and got 'Yes that is fine'. Then at 11:28, four minutes later, she asked the only question that mattered: 'Hi money had been very very low for a while now is there anything the team is doing to help this what’s the next step?' and tagged '@mmayson'. Thirty-five seconds later Mayson answered: 'Let’s hop on a call tomorrow and go over it!'. Her reply, thirty-two seconds after that, is the epitaph for this account: 'Okay but we did this already nothing Has been changed since?'. Eighty-six minutes later she terminated. That was the THIRD call offered in eighteen days (Sept 3/4, Sept 11, Sept 21) and the seventh escalation of the same growth-and-revenue complaint since May 20. Not one of those calls ever produced a single written word, a figure, or a named person in the chat. Her 2026-09-02 message — editing 'quite poor', same songs reused, ~150 views a post, a rival agency taking a peer to ~40k followers on the identical brief, and a direct request that ALTR put a named specialist on her two accounts — died at 23 days unanswered and was never answered at all. Her 2026-09-15 request, 'Hi can I see some updates and proof of Facebook advertising please as I feel like none has been done for ages', died at 10 days unanswered and was never answered at all. Last week's report said in writing that if another window passed without her chasing, this should be escalated to Derrek as a churn risk. She did chase, once, on Sept 21 — and was offered a fourth meeting instead of an answer. Everything else in the window is the sound of an account that had already stopped running: Derrek zero messages (12 days silent, 55 days since his last substantive post), Vivek zero messages (18 days, still hospitalised, no cover ever named, the 'can’t go live' restriction never verified), Michelle zero messages and her weekly leak-removal report now missed for a SECOND consecutive week (17 days since Sept 8, against a cadence that never missed between Jul 1 and Sept 8), Mica Vecco zero messages with the restored reel drop due around Sept 22 and never delivered, Stephski zero messages including in the 3 days 20 hours since a paying client asked her for a final invoice. The commercial exposure is immediate and it is small but real: she has been billed only to 2026-09-14. The Sept 15 to Sept 21 revenue is unbilled, she asked for the invoice herself, she said she would pay it 'straight away', and she has paid all ten previous invoices with an average of about two days and the last one in two hours and one minute. That money is collectable today and gets less collectable every day the chat stays silent. Also unresolved at exit: the Instagram password she pasted into this group chat on 2026-09-07 at Vivek's request (Amber_hazee / [REDACTED-PASSWORD]) has still never been confirmed rotated — 18 days — and ALTR still holds the logins to her main and both management-run Instagram accounts. Wesley's anniversary sends from Aug 11 and Aug 14 have now left the engagement with zero trace in 1,137 messages. Nothing about her tone was hostile. She said 'you guys have been great' and offered to pay on the way out. That is not a dispute. It is a client who separated her obligations from her expectations months ago, kept meeting the obligations, and left the moment somebody offered her an alternative.

health.rationale: Down 30 from 35. The client terminated the engagement on 2026-09-21 and ALTR has not replied to the termination notice in the 3 days and 20 hours to the window close. There is no partial credit available here. The score is not 0 only because the exit is clean rather than hostile — 'Thank you for everything you guys have been great' — she asked for the final invoice herself and volunteered to pay it immediately, there is no dispute, no chargeback, no threat, no public complaint, and ten of ten invoices were paid with the most recent settling in two hours. A relationship that ends with the client offering to pay is one that can in principle be salvaged or at least offboarded without loss. Everything else is failure. The churn was signalled, in writing, in this report's own file, seven times: the growth-and-marketing complaint escalated on 2026-05-20, 2026-06-02, 2026-06-04, 2026-07-21, 2026-09-02, 2026-09-15 and finally 2026-09-21. Last week's report named the exact trigger — 'if another window passes with her not chasing the Instagram complaint, escalate to Derrek as a churn risk regardless of tone or payment behaviour' — and named the exact cheapest fix, a weekly numbers post. Neither happened. Her final question on Sept 21, 'Hi money had been very very low for a while now is there anything the team is doing to help this what’s the next step?', was answered in thirty-five seconds with 'Let’s hop on a call tomorrow and go over it!' — the third call offer in eighteen days, after two previous calls that produced no written outcome of any kind. Her response, 'Okay but we did this already nothing Has been changed since?', is a client stating that the agency's only response mechanism has already failed twice. She churned eighty-six minutes later. At the moment of exit: her Sept 2 staffing complaint was 23 days unanswered and was never answered; her Sept 15 request for proof of Facebook advertising was 10 days unanswered and was never answered; Derrek's Aug 2 Meta-rep cost question was 54 days unanswered; his Aug 1 promise of weekly phone-farm updates was 55 days old with one uncaptioned screenshot as its entire output; the block list she called 'very important' on May 10 was 138 days unactioned; Wesley's Aug 11 and Aug 14 anniversary sends were 45 and 42 days unconfirmed; the Moggy damage control was 49 days; in four and a half months she was never given one follower, view, reach or spend figure for accounts ALTR ran on her behalf. Four of the six people on this account sent zero messages in the window, including the owner, and the two proactive deliverables that had been restored the week before — Michelle's leak report and Mica's reel drop — both stopped again. The account did not collapse this week. It finished collapsing this week.
